items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: Billy Hart is such a strong drummer. You had to be that to give Wes what he was calling for.

ctx.x: another one in for us to play, maybe something we really liked. It could be "Tenderly" or some kind of ballad thing. "Rainy Day" or something, and then he'd sneak some of these other things in. But he got them in in the course of the night, he kept the people really satisfied.

I was still fighting this image of trying to play the upright bass. I wasn't that unhappy with it at this point, but I just couldn't get...Here I am complaining again. Because the sound was so strong. When you think about how firm and heavy Wes played, with the congas...and Buddy was a strong player, he still is. It was like there was no way in the world I could... With the congas, and the drums. Billy Hart is such a strong drummer. You had to be that to give Wes what he was calling for. I just got drowned in it.

So now I got me a big amplifier and a big bass, and I'm carrying these two, just so I can cut through with this thing, right? One day I was saying, I was just tired of lugging them and I had to be...The hassle of traveling that way was really hard on me. And I said to Wes once, we were in Pittsburgh, 'Hey, man, it's not the same thing. Every time I change rhythm the sound changes, the least little thing, if I got a crack in my bass of something, or the amplifier, or there's not room on the stage, or there's…
